solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Article seen by chief is to come

parts.note: A is the indefinite article
a head is a chief or leader

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece read by the boss is still to be published.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ahead lies in the future, still awaiting us, as with the worst being yet ahead.

clue.text: Mood cheers up with doctor on department

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: ta is British informal thanks, like cheers
MO is a medical officer, an army doctor
a sphere is a field or department of activity

explanation.surface: A gloomy atmosphere lifts when a doctor joins the department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cheers up' reads as brightening, but in this down clue 'up' reverses the British thank-you word, giving AT.
explanation.definitionFit: The atmosphere of a place is its prevailing feeling or tone, its mood.

clue.text: Musical talent gets attention

definitions.meaning: to have an ... for music is to have musical talent
to have someone's ... is to have their attention

explanation.surface: A gifted musician wins notice.
explanation.definitionFit: An ear is both a knack for hearing music and, in 'lend an ear', a listener's attention.

clue.text: Miserable face sergeant-major wears

indicators.note: the face wears the officer like clothing, so his letters sit inside it

parts.note: a dial is the face of a clock or meter

explanation.surface: A sergeant-major goes about with a glum expression.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismal and miserable are synonyms, both meaning gloomy and wretched.

clue.text: Fail to get great deal that would assist higher aims?

parts.note: to bomb is to fail badly, as a show bombs
a sight is informal for a lot, as in a sight better

explanation.surface: Someone misses out on a big bargain that would help their lofty ambitions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'higher aims' is literal: the device helps a bomber crew aim from high in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: A bombsight is the aiming instrument in a bomber aircraft, helping crews target from altitude.

clue.text: Swimsuits composer carried across East River

indicators.note: the composer carries the compass point over his middle, holding it inside

parts.note: Johann Sebastian Bach, the composer
the Wear is a river in north-east England, flowing through Durham

explanation.surface: A composer takes swimwear over to the east bank of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Beachwear is clothing for the seaside, chiefly bathing costumes.

clue.text: Staff outside the Italian financial centre

indicators.note: the staffing word goes around the outside of the Italian article

parts.note: to man a post is to staff it
il is Italian for the

explanation.surface: Employees work outside the Italian stock exchange.
explanation.definitionFit: Milan is Italy's business hub, home to its stock exchange.

clue.text: Runner showing increased complacency circling lake

indicators.note: the comparative goes round the letter for the lake, enclosing it

parts.note: smugger means more complacent

explanation.surface: An athlete grows more self-satisfied with every lap of the lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runner' suggests an athlete, but it means one who runs contraband.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner is one who carries goods illegally, as in gun-runner, which is a smuggler.

clue.text: Documents for discussion in genre slammed by media

indicators.note: a genre slammed is knocked about, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the papers are the print news media

explanation.surface: Documents about a literary genre are panned by the press.
explanation.definitionFit: A green paper is a UK government consultation document, issued to prompt debate before policy is fixed.

clue.text: Boozer turned on initially amenable canine

indicators.note: turned means the word for the drinker is reversed

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunk

indicators.note: initially means take the opening letter of amenable

explanation.surface: A drunk turns on a dog that started off friendly.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tosa is a large Japanese breed of dog, originally bred for fighting.

clue.text: Correspondence about a break in cloud

indicators.note: the post wraps about the other pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: mail is letters, correspondence
a rest is a break

explanation.surface: Letters arrive about a gap in the cloud cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Mare's tails are long wispy streaks of high cirrus cloud.

clue.text: Escorts abandoning hotel customers

indicators.note: abandoning means the letter for hotel is left out

parts.note: ushers escort people to their seats
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Escorts leave the hotel's clients.
explanation.definitionFit: Users of a service or product are its customers or clients.

clue.text: Star hides much being a deranged killer

indicators.note: the star hides the scrambled letters inside itself

parts.note: the Sun is our star

indicators.note: deranged means disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A celebrity conceals a lot, being a crazed murderer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' is our own star here, not a celebrity; 'deranged' scrambles three clue words into BMACHINEGU, and 'hides' tucks that between SU and N.
explanation.definitionFit: A submachine gun is a lightweight automatic weapon, a deadly instrument, so a killer.

clue.text: Monk one taking place in church service

parts.note: St Benedict, the monk who founded the Benedictine order
I is the Roman numeral for one
on means happening, as in the show is on

explanation.surface: A monk takes his place in a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: Benediction is a short Catholic devotional service in which the congregation is blessed with the Eucharist.

clue.text: Peaceful border in Asian region

parts.note: pacific means peaceful
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: A calm frontier in a part of Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pacific Rim is the ring of lands around the Pacific Ocean, including East Asia.

clue.text: Henry sort of cross with horse coming first

indicators.note: the drug's letter comes to the front of the cross word

parts.note: an ankh is an Egyptian cross with a loop at the top
horse is slang for heroin, abbreviated H

explanation.surface: Henry is somewhat annoyed that a horse finished in front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' looks like 'angry' and 'horse' like an animal; one is the ankh, the other heroin.
explanation.definitionFit: Hank is a familiar American nickname for someone named Henry, as with Hank Williams.

clue.text: Those wanted are dead? It's uncertain

indicators.note: uncertain means not fixed, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Are the wanted fugitives dead? Nobody can be sure.
explanation.definitionFit: Desiderata is Latin for things desired, the plural of desideratum, so things wanted.

clue.text: Corrupt state? On the contrary

parts.note: the condition opposite to being corrupt: purity and freedom from guilt

explanation.surface: A rotten regime? Quite the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corrupt state' first reads as a crooked country; reversing the idea gives an uncorrupted condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Innocence is freedom from sin or guilt, the very opposite of a depraved condition.

clue.text: Zealot on charter round island promoting growth

parts.note: a nut is an enthusiast, a fanatic

indicators.note: the hiring word goes round the island letter

parts.note: to rent a boat or plane is to charter it

explanation.surface: A fanatic charters a boat around an island to boost development.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutrient as an adjective describes something nourishing, which feeds and so fosters development.

clue.text: Tirade on socialist dog is something fruity

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after the preceding pieces

parts.note: red is a common label for a socialist
a cur is a mongrel dog
a rant is a tirade

explanation.surface: A rant about a left-wing mongrel is rather spicy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fruity' suggests risqué, but here it means a fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The redcurrant is a small red berry grown on bushes, a soft fruit.

clue.text: Despite everything one finds legendary creature

parts.note: yet means nevertheless, despite everything
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Against all odds, someone discovers a mythical beast.
explanation.definitionFit: The yeti, or abominable snowman, is a creature of Himalayan folklore.

clue.text: Bower Eliza Doolittle's refuge?

indicators.note: Eliza Doolittle, the Cockney flower girl of Pygmalion and My Fair Lady, drops her aitches

parts.note: a harbour is a refuge or shelter

explanation.surface: A leafy bower is the shelter of the flower girl from My Fair Lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eliza Doolittle's' says the word is said in Cockney, where an initial H is dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbour is a shady garden shelter of trees or climbing plants, a bower.

clue.text: Rozzer has run inside: crime writer almost catching us in college

indicators.note: the policeman piece catches up with us, so it is placed right before it
the run letter is put inside the police word

parts.note: rozzer is old British slang for a policeman, a cop
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the writer's name is dropped

parts.note: Agatha Christie, the crime novelist

explanation.surface: A policeman nabs a runner while Agatha Christie nearly corners us at a college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' gives CORP; 'catching' just places US next; 'almost' drops the final E of the novelist's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Corpus Christi is the name of colleges at both Oxford and Cambridge.

clue.text: Duke leaves South African port for city

definitions.note: used attributively, as in city life, matching the adjective

indicators.note: the duke leaves, so his letter is taken out

parts.note: Durban is a port in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa

explanation.surface: A duke departs a South African port for a city elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Urban describes things belonging to towns, as city streets are urban streets.

clue.text: Majestic European prince appearing regularly

indicators.note: appearing regularly means take every other letter of prince, starting with the first

explanation.surface: A grand European prince makes frequent appearances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appearing regularly' takes the odd letters of PRINCE: P, I, C.
explanation.definitionFit: Epic means grand and heroic in scale, as is anything majestic.

clue.text: Best quality piano introducing old poem

indicators.note: the piano letter introduces the poem, so it stands in front

parts.note: p is the musical notation for piano, soft
rime is an old spelling of rhyme, as in Coleridge's Rime of the Ancient Mariner

explanation.surface: The finest piano accompanies the reading of an old poem.
explanation.definitionFit: Prime means first-rate, of the highest grade, as in prime beef.

clue.text: Broad line curls round belt

indicators.note: the words curl round into a new shape, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A thick line bends round a waist.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandolier is a shoulder belt with loops or pockets for carrying cartridges.

clue.text: Operatic role thought to release energy

indicators.note: to release means let the letter for energy go, so it is removed

parts.note: an idea is a thought
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A part in an opera is thought to free up energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ida is the title character of Gilbert and Sullivan's comic opera Princess Ida.

clue.text: Lady of the Lake

definitions.meaning: Lake ... lies on the borders of Germany, Austria and Switzerland

explanation.surface: The Lady of the Lake, from Arthurian legend.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes Arthurian legend's Lady of the Lake, but the lady is a name and the lake is a real one.
explanation.definitionFit: Constance is a female first name and also the English name of the Bodensee lake.

clue.text: Silver coin added to millions in kingdom

parts.note: the real was an old Spanish silver coin
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A silver coin is added to millions in the kingdom's treasury.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a kingdom, the domain ruled by a monarch.
